definitions.amount_proxy: volume x mean(open, high, low, close), the predictor's expression
definitions.floats: float() of the stored decimal strings
definitions.predictor_normalisation: float32 channels, per-window mean and population std over the 512 rows, (x - mean) / (std + 1e-5), clipped at +-5 (KronosPredictor at the vendored commit)
definitions.return: r_t = ln(close_t / close_(t-1h)) where t and t - 1h exist in both sources

derived.returns/one_minus_pearson: 1 - pearson; its interval is the transform of pearson's
derived.returns/one_minus_spearman: 1 - spearman; its interval is the transform of spearman's

figures: figures/mismatch_return_scatter.png: r_bingx against r_binance in bp
figures/mismatch_price_differences.png: histograms of the signed price differences
figures/mismatch_agreement.png: A_x, A_f, A_xd and the paired differences with intervals (Kronos part only)

intervals.blocks: calendar weeks starting Monday 00:00 UTC for hourly series; groups of 4 calendar weeks (Monday 00:00 UTC grid) for the 61-hour Kronos sample (also the dz of the amount section)
intervals.paired: paired comparisons resample both columns in one call
intervals.quantiles: medians get an interval unless their bootstrap distribution is a single value; p90, p99 and max are descriptive
intervals.seed: numpy seed = first 4 bytes of sha256('kronos-agent/bootstrap/v1/' + key), key = 'mismatch/<section>/<statistic>'
intervals.shares: a share of exactly 0 or 1 gets a Wilson interval at the number of blocks; deff and n_eff are reported for shares

kronos.agreement: agree(a, b) = the two signals are equal
kronos.blocks: groups of 4 calendar weeks (Monday 00:00 UTC grid)

fallback.rule: the same with a 97-hour step, only if the owner declines the compute

gate3.rule: the estimate (cpu_seconds = pending fans x seconds per fan x threads) is measured before any fan; above the limit the batch runs only with --approved-by-owner CPU_HOURS, the figure the owner approved, and only when the measured CPU-hours are at most the tolerance times it; every batch that computes fans appends its record (approved figure, estimate, config_id, design, dropped tasks, the command's start) to mismatch.gate3.jsonl beside the report before its first fan, and the report lists every record of the forecast config of its fans

kronos.hours_used: an hour enters only with its three fans (both windows complete)

sample.planned: 873 fans, about 1.5 CPU-hours (3.15 s per fan measured on 2026-11-01)
sample.rule: D_k = 2024-07-01T00:00Z + 61 k h while D_k < 2026-07-10T08:00Z (every hour of the day)

kronos.signal: sign of mean_k(close[k, N]) / close[D - 1h] - 1 at N = horizon_n; p_up = share of trajectories whose close at N is strictly above close[D - 1h]
kronos.status_rule: computed by `mismatch --kronos` behind gate 3; a run without --kronos rebuilds it from the stored fans when every fan of a pre-registered sample (the primary one first, then the fallback) is stored under the current forecast config, and otherwise reports that it has not run

range.rule: every hour present in both sources from the start of the BingX real-market history to the sealed start; candles read through read_study_frame as decimal strings, opening before the sealed start; contemporaneous candles of two venues, no validation outcome is involved

reading_rules: alignment: the report fails unless the lag-0 return correlation is larger than the correlation at every other lag in -2..+2 h

kronos: an interval of kronos/a_x_minus_a_f entirely above 0 reads 'the data effect is smaller than seed noise', entirely below 0 'the data effect is larger than seed noise'; an interval containing 0, or no interval, 'not distinguishable'

kronos: an interval of kronos/a_xd_minus_a_f entirely below 0 reads 'the sources shift the signal beyond seed noise' (SPEC section 5: say so), entirely above 0 'the cross-source pair agrees more often than the two-seed floor'; an interval containing 0, or no interval, 'not distinguishable'
every reading is printed with the minimum detectable difference: (z_0.975 + z_0.80) x the standard error read from the 95 % interval, (high - low) / (2 z_0.975)
